title: Water Cycle Basics
summary: This lesson explores how water moves above and below the Earth's surface through the continuous process of the water cycle. Students will learn the key stages including evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection.

sections.text: Scene: A diagram showing a wide blue ocean below with arrows pointing upwards toward a bright yellow sun, and a blue liquid droplet transforming into a wispy cloud shape higher up. I wonder...?: How does water move above and below the Earth's surface? Answer: The water cycle describes how water moves above and below the Earth's surface through a continuous loop.

Scene: A visual of heat radiating from the sun onto liquid water, turning it into rising vapor that cools into clouds high in the sky. I wonder...?: What turns liquid water into vapor? Answer: Evaporation turns liquid water into vapor using heat from the sun, and condensation forms clouds when vapor cools high in the sky.

Scene: A picture of gray clouds releasing white snowflakes and blue raindrops downward, which flow into rivers, lakes, and oceans. I wonder...?: How does water return to the Earth? Answer: Precipitation returns water as rain or snow, and collection gathers runoff into rivers, lakes, and oceans.

learning_objectives: Describe how water moves above and below the Earth's surface
Explain the processes of evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection
